scenario: AITA for telling my father to fuck off for telling me I need to get my daughter into basketball? | I feel like I was too harsh and even my husband thinks I could have done it better but I feel like that's partly because he hasn't felt the full weight of my father's micromanagement. Growing up I had certain interests, I was VERY into these activities. Around the time I was in the 8th grade my sister got jealous of the success I was having in this area. After that point I was strongly "discouraged" from taking part in these activities unless it was at school. Instead they pushed me to work with children. They told me it was my gift (super Christian family) and that I shouldn't squander my talent. So there's the background on why I think I responded so strongly. My youngest daughter is tall and always has been. She's 11 years old and 5'6" and is still growing. Starting at about age 5? My father has pushed me to make her do basketball. Because she's tall, I mean let's ignore the fact that she inherited my clumsy gene, that she's a very shy girl, that she hates crowds and noise. Ugh. Anyway a few days ago I made a rare visit to my parent's house, I felt it was safe because family friends were there. I was bemoaning the utter lack of art day camps or just evening classes. All three of my girls love art so I'm looking for something that they will actually enjoy. My father brought up fucking basketball again. "You need to get youngest daughter into it, who cares if she doesn't want to. You're the parent just tell her she's doing it." Honestly it brought up a lot of really shitty feelings that I didn't realize were still hanging around. I got up grabbed my purse and told him he could fuck off and left. So reddit am I the asshole for my reaction here? Was I overreacting? I'm really torn here, I'm generally a people pleaser but I really don't think I was out of line and I'm certainly not going to apologize, because I'm not really sorry. Which makes me wonder if I'm an asshole for not apologizing.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was being an asshole when I told my father to fuck off for telling me to get my daughter into basketball. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, there's a lot of background here. I grew up in a super Christian family where my talents were supposed to be used for working with children. My sister got jealous of my success in certain activities, and that led to me being discouraged from pursuing those interests unless it was at school. Now, as an adult, I have a daughter who is tall, but she's also shy, hates crowds and noise, and inherited my clumsy genes. My father has been pushing me to get her into basketball because of her height, ignoring her personality and other interests. A few days ago, I visited my parents' house with some family friends. I was complaining about the lack of art day camps or evening classes for my girls, who all love art. My father brought up basketball again, saying I should just make my daughter do it regardless of her feelings. This triggered a lot of old, negative feelings for me, and I ended up telling him to fuck off and left. Now, I'm wondering if I was being an asshole for reacting that way. I generally try to please people, but I don't think I was out of line here. I'm not sorry for what I did, but I'm still torn because I don't want to be the asshole. Let me break this down. My father's behavior seems controlling and dismissive of my daughter's feelings and interests. He's pushing basketball based solely on her height, ignoring her personality and other talents. That's problematic because it doesn't respect her as an individual. On the other hand, I reacted by telling him to fuck off and leaving. That's a strong reaction. While I understand why I did it, it might have been over the top. My husband thinks I could have handled it better, which makes me wonder if I was too harsh. But then, I remember the background of being micromanaged and discouraged from pursuing my own interests as a child. That must have contributed to my strong reaction. It's like my father's behavior triggered old wounds, making me react more intensely than I might have otherwise. So, was I being an asshole? Well, calling someone to fuck off is definitely harsh and disrespectful. It's not the best way to handle the situation, especially in front of family friends. However, I can see why I did it given the history of being controlled and having my interests dismissed. Maybe a better approach would have been to calmly explain why I don't think basketball is the right fit for my daughter, without resorting to such strong language. That way, I could have stood my ground without being disrespectful. But I also have to consider my feelings and boundaries. It's important to stand up for myself and my daughter, especially when someone is being controlling. However, there's a balance between asserting myself and maintaining respectful communication. In the end, I think I was partly in the right for standing up against my father's controlling behavior, but the way I did it was too harsh. It's okay to set boundaries, but the language I used crossed a line. I should have found a more constructive way to express my feelings and protect my daughter's interests without being disrespectful. So, to answer the question: Was I being an asshole? I think there's a bit of both. I had valid reasons for reacting strongly, but the way I expressed it was over the top and disrespectful. It would have been better to handle the situation more calmly and assertively without the harsh language.
